facts.evidence: Reported earnings of $12.1 billion for the second quarter 2026.
Record U.S. production; worldwide production increased 20% from last year.
Total debt reduced by $8.4 billion, to $37,075 million, strengthening the balance sheet.

claims.claim: Reported earnings were $12.1 billion for second quarter 2026.
Return on capital employed (ROCE) was 21.4%.
U.S. production was a record.
Worldwide production increased 20% from last year.
Crude unit throughput at U.S. refineries was a record 1.07 million barrels per day.
Chevron signed a 20-year power agreement with Microsoft for a West Texas data center.
U.S. Upstream earnings were $3,541 million.
U.S. Upstream earnings were up 73% from the year-ago period.
claims.note: Release prints no growth rate; the computed change from 2Q25 earnings of $1,418 million is about +150%, not 73%.

claims.claim: U.S. Upstream earnings were driven by higher liquids realizations and sales volumes.
International Upstream earnings were $4,641 million.
International Upstream earnings were up 221% from the year-ago period.
claims.note: Release prints no growth rate; the computed change from 2Q25 earnings of $1,309 million is about +255%, not 221%.

claims.claim: International Upstream earnings rose due to higher sales volumes and liquids realizations.
U.S. Downstream earnings were $2,411 million.
U.S. Downstream earnings were up 481% from the year-ago period.
claims.note: Release prints no growth rate; the computed change from 2Q25 earnings of $404 million is about +497%, not 481%.

claims.claim: U.S. Downstream earnings rose primarily due to higher margins on refined product sales.
International Downstream earnings were $2,457 million.
International Downstream earnings were up 197% from the year-ago period.
claims.note: Release prints no growth rate; the computed change from 2Q25 earnings of $333 million is about +638%, not 197%.

claims.claim: International Downstream earnings were driven by higher margins on refined product sales and an asset sale gain.
No guidance or outlook was provided in the release.
claims.note: Release does contain forward-looking targets, notably a structural cost reduction program that 'aims to reduce structural costs by $3-4 billion by the end of 2026' and a Singapore divestment 'expected to close in 2027'; it also points to a separately published 'Sensitivities and Forward Guidance' document. A blanket 'no outlook' overstates the case.

claims.claim: Total debt was reduced by $8.4 billion.
Total debt stood at $37,075 million.
The debt reduction strengthened the balance sheet.
Net debt-to-CFFO ratio was 0.6x.
The net debt-to-CFFO ratio of 0.6x indicates strong cash generation.
